Assessment of Community Engaged Learning 
Each year the Leduc Center surveys students across all the colleges to determine the impact of 
CEL classes on civic knowledge, skills, and abilities; class learning objectives; and desire to stay at 
UMassD. This academic year we surveyed 204 students. 
College participants in Table I reported increases in their civic skills following their participation in 
community-engaged learning classes. The following table shows the difference in the civic skills of 
participants before and after program participation. The means below are based on a 5-point scale; 
with 1 being “I cannot do this at all” to 5 being “I can do this very well.” Mean scores of skills before 
and after program participation were compared using a paired sample t-test. 
The t-test shows that there is a positive relationship between participation in the community- 
engaged learning classes and reported gains in civic skills related to addressing social problems. As 
Table 1 indicates, all the civic skills were statistically significant at the .001 level. This clearly indicates 
the positive impact students believe community-engaged learning has had on their ability to use 
their UMass Dartmouth education to meet community needs presently and in the future.
